name: Cost and rate
usage: Declare every paid service once with its monthly cap: const services = paidServices([{ name: "openai", unit: "usd-cents", monthlyCap: 5000 }]) (amounts are whole numbers in the service's unit; there is no default cap, because how much may be spent is the app owner's decision). Create one meter: const meter = costMeter({ services, store: pgStore(query) }) (the paid_usage table, PAID_USAGE_SQL, in a migration, so every instance counts against the same cap; memoryStore() is for one process and tests), with timeZone set to the month the budget counts in (default UTC). Make every paid call through it: await meter.charge("openai", estimate, async () => { const r = await callProvider(); return { cost: realCost, ...r }; }). A call that would pass the cap throws CapExceededError (code cap-exceeded, status 429) before it runs, so it spends nothing; answer the user with that status. A failed call keeps its estimate (it may have been billed). Serve await meter.report() (month, and per service unit, monthlyCap, spent, remaining) to the project budget. The review (SM-12-L1) checks that no paid SDK is called outside meter.charge.
